title: Rollback sensitivity scoring and state harmonizer for config changes
creator: Aisha Tan
description:
Problem: Config changes to batching, KV caching, and routing policies sometimes cause transient cost spikes or tail-latency regressions that are hard to detect until a full rollout completes. Existing mechanisms can either be too aggressive (immediate rollback on a single alert) or too slow (manual rollback after customer tickets).

Objective: Build an automated rollback system that scores the risk/sensitivity of each config change, triggers safe, staged applies, detects regressions across cost/latency/quality signals, and reconciles desired vs actual state while preserving auditability and operational control. The feature should operate across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with consistent semantics.

High-level approach:
1) Sensitivity scoring: compute a per-change sensitivity score composed of factors including change surface area (e.g., batching window, KV cache TTL, quantization profile), historical variance on affected routes/models, customer tier, and deploy topology (canary percentage, capacity tier). Scores map to rollout policies (fast, staged, manual) and rollback thresholds.
2) Simulation & preflight: run a dry-run risk simulation in sandboxed canary traffic using replay traces (from traffic capture) and a cost delta estimator to predict expected token/sec and cost changes before applying broadly. If simulation indicates > X% cost increase or SLA risk, flag for manual review.
3) Runtime triggers: observable-driven triggers include: sustained cost-per-token delta, moving-average request latency SLI breach, increased error rates, and served-output quality regressions (as measured by automated evals on a prompt set). Each trigger emits a weighted signal; combined signals above the dynamic threshold initiate rollback.
4) Guardrails & hysteresis: implement multi-window checks (1m/5m/30m), minimum evaluation window, cooldown periods after rollbacks, and human-in-loop pause for high-sensitivity changes. Allow configured tolerance per customer/route.
5) State harmonizer & reconciliation: maintain a canonical desired config in the control plane and a versioned actual state observed from agents. Periodic reconcilers detect drift, attempt automated re-apply with exponential backoff, and escalate if immutable drift is observed. Reconciler must be idempotent and handle partial-apply situations (e.g., some shards applied, others not).
6) Safe apply paths: staged canaries (10% -> 30% -> 100%), capacity-aware routing (avoid concentrating canaries on a single GPU pool), and emergency fallbacks to compatible model variants or previous config snapshots.
7) Auditability & runbooks: every automatic rollback must produce an audit record with root-cause signals, snapshot of before/after configs, links to coroners (logs, traces, cost dashboards), and a recommended revert PR if human review is needed. Include links to the runbook (Confluence) and SWAT channel.

Architecture notes: a lightweight scorer service will run as part of the control plane and annotate change requests with sensitivity metadata. The orchestrator interacts with serving agents via the existing config apply API; the reconciler is a separate component that subscribes to agent state via the events bus. All decisions must be reversible and logged in the existing audit log with immutable IDs.

Testing plan: unit tests for scoring logic, integration tests that replay captured traffic in a staging runtime, chaos tests that simulate partial apply and delayed agent responses, and load tests to validate that auto-rollbacks don't cascade into flapping.

Operational acceptance criteria and runbook entries are included in the attached design doc: https://confluence.redwoodinfra/internal/config-safety/rollback-harmonizer and prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6189.

Notes on privacy/compliance: for Private/VPC installs, the reconciler will respect local policy and will default to manual rollback for air-gapped environments unless explicit consent is configured.

Open questions: how to incorporate model-quality regressions that are costly to measure in real-time, and whether we should surface the sensitivity score to customers via the Console for transparency.

acceptance_criteria: Sensitivity scoring computed for each config change and persisted as metadata before any rollout.
Dry-run simulation runs for staged canaries using captured traces and emits predicted cost/latency deltas.
Automatic rollback triggers when combined weighted signal crosses configured threshold and performs safe revert to previous snapshot with audit record.
Reconciler detects and resolves drift or escalates after N failed reapply attempts with clear error categorization.
No customer-facing downtime caused by automated rollbacks in 10k+ request/min test; rollbacks complete within configured cooldown window.
Runbook and postmortem template created and linked in Confluence; on-call notified automatically on rollback events.
